params.why: the given angle at Z must be acute (Y lies higher than Z) and a clean size
the two corresponding angles must not coincide, so the reasons cannot be confused
the angle between the extensions must be a sensible, non-tiny size

stem: $AB$ and $DC$ are parallel lines, both drawn vertically: $A$ and $D$ are at the top, $B$ and $C$ are at the bottom, and $DC$ is to the right of $AB$. The points $X$ and $Z$ lie on $AB$, with $X$ above $Z$. The point $Y$ lies on $DC$, lower than $X$ and higher than $Z$. The straight lines $XY$ and $ZY$ are drawn, and each is extended beyond $Y$ to the right of $DC$: $ZY$ is extended to a point $P$ and $XY$ is extended to a point $Q$ (so $P$ lies above $Q$). It is given that $A\hat{Z}Y = {=p}^\circ$, $B\hat{X}Y = x^\circ$ and $P\hat{Y}Q = ({=c}x - {=d})^\circ$. Calculate the value of $x$.
solution: $D\hat{Y}P = A\hat{Z}Y = {=p}^\circ$ (corresponding angles; $AB \parallel DC$), because $ZYP$ is a straight line crossing both parallel lines.
$Q\hat{Y}C = B\hat{X}Y = x^\circ$ (corresponding angles; $AB \parallel DC$), because $XYQ$ is a straight line crossing both parallel lines.
$D\hat{Y}P + P\hat{Y}Q + Q\hat{Y}C = 180^\circ$ (angles on a straight line $DC$), so ${=p}^\circ + ({=c}x - {=d})^\circ + x^\circ = 180^\circ$.
notes: Text-only restatement of book exercise 7.1 q3 (two lines through a point Y on one parallel line; corresponding angles at Y, then angles on a straight line, then a linear equation). The book's figure is replaced by an explicit layout in words: vertical parallels, X above Z on AB, Y on DC between them in height, P above Q on the extensions beyond Y. Given angles p (at Z) and x (at X) are both acute, which forces Y between the two heights, so the layout is consistent for every instance; I checked this numerically with coordinates for all 898 admissible parameter sets. The equation (c+1)x = 180 - p + d is also what the triangle route gives (P-Y-Q is vertically opposite X-Y-Z), so a solver using either method reaches the same x. Parameters are built backwards from x, so x is always a whole number between 30 and 70 and the angle c*x - d is positive.
